name: the failed-only retry asks about every entity again
why: F7 itself: dropping the filter restores _relRetryAll()'s behaviour, so recovering three failures costs a request per row. The test asserts an EXACT count against the failure count, so this cannot be satisfied by luck.

name: the failed-only retry asks about nothing
why: The other direction, and the reason the test does not settle for "fewer requests than before": a retry that issues nothing at all would pass a count-went-down assertion while leaving every failed cell unrecovered. Pinned by the companion icon assertion.

name: the count ignores the source rows
why: The trap this design turns on. runFilter() REMOVES non-matching rows, so a live-DOM-only tally loses the failures a filter is hiding — and the retry then leaves them marked failed, which the impl's candidate scan and _relQueueStillWants() both read as "leave alone", stranding them for good. Pinned through __saTest.relFailedMbids() rather than the button's label: the label is repainted only on a cell write, so a filter alone never recomputes it and a label assertion would measure "the button was not repainted" instead. An earlier draft of the spec did exactly that and this mutation passed against it.

name: an entity answered elsewhere is retried anyway
why: KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden: every MBID appears exactly once on this fixture, so the done-wins rule is never exercised and no assertion here can see it. It matters on a page that lists the same entity twice, and on the live/master pair during the window before _relWriteResult() has mirrored its answer — re-requesting an entity already answered is the waste this whole change removes. Covering it needs a fixture with a repeated entity; none of the committed ones has one.

name: the reload-everything button becomes failed-only too
why: "Force a genuine refetch of a table I believe is stale" is a different intent from "recover the failures", and the org says both are legitimate. Collapsing them is the plausible future simplification; this is what has to fail when someone tries it.

name: a single-table page loses its retry anchor again
why: The pre-existing bug this branch fixed in passing: the walk stopped at the <h2>, so on a single-table page with cover art off the retry buttons were built and then dropped on the floor — which is every single-table FIXTURE, and why no spec had ever seen them. The failed-only control anchors on them, so it goes missing too.
